newsitem.title: NORWAY: DnB ups bid for BNbank to 209 NOK.
newsitem.headline: DnB ups bid for BNbank to 209 NOK.

text.p: Den norske Bank ASA, Norway's largest bank, said on Wednesday it was raising its bid for mortgage lender Bolig og Naeringsbanken (BNbank) to 209 crowns from 207 crowns per share, both cash offers including 1996 dividend.
The 1996 dividend at BNbank is 10.50 crowns.
It said the reason for the upgrading was that DnB from April 3 to 11 bought options for 2,788,820 shares in BNbank.
"The bank has undertaken a total evaluation of the price of a possible obligatory bid, and has valued this at 209 crowns per share in BNbank," the brief statement said.

The mortgage lender last week inclined towards accepting DnB's bid but no decision has yet been made. There is also a rival bid from Fokus Bank, which last month made a share exchange offer pricing BNbank at 2.06 billion crowns.

The new DnB bid valued BNbank at 2.04 billion crowns. It was the third offer from DnB since the takeover battle began last month with a bid by Fokus, which has since become target of a hostile takeover attempt by Sparebankgruppen, a group of savings banks.
BNbank shareholders were previously given until the end of April to accept a DnB bid.

BNbank's biggest shareholder, financial institution Den Nordenfjelske Bykredittforening, announced last week it was accepting DnB's 207 crowns bid and was prepared to sell its 10 percent stake to DnB.
DnB's bid is conditional of DnB acquiring more than 90 percent of BNbank, that regulatory authorities approve of the acquisition and that no significant changes occur in BNbank's financial position.
